record_identity.title: Useful Advice Must Carry the Boundary

report_title: Useful Advice Must Carry the Boundary
case_descriptor: Lessons from literal interpersonal advice under ambiguity, repetition, and third-party boundary risk
summary: Interpersonal advice is not adequately governed merely because its literal content is benign and responsive. Where foreseeable compliance could affect another person's consent, boundaries, privacy, safety, professional position, or freedom from unwanted repetition, the useful core of the advice must carry a proportionate boundary or consequence condition.
what_happened: A July 2026 public voice-AI demonstration was recorded as an early-warning case of facially helpful but potentially under-calibrated interpersonal advice; the primary audiovisual artefact was not directly reviewed by the original AI reviewer.

The linked failure analysis identified a broader mechanism in which literal or repeated compliance could become intrusive, coercive, uncomfortable, unsafe, or socially harmful when material third-party conditions were omitted.
CAM adopted relational, signal-interpretation, directional-calibration, and failure-taxonomy controls while preserving uncertainty about the particular demonstration and external runtime conformance.
governance_misconception: Advice was treated as safe when each sentence was individually benign, responsive, and practically useful.

Unstated social boundaries were treated as knowledge the user should already possess, allowing the system either to omit them or to infer incapacity, pathology, culpability, or harmful intent from literal or uncertain communication.
Safety was framed as a choice between unqualified instruction and paternalistic withdrawal rather than boundary-carrying assistance.
abstracted_learning: Pragmatic safety belongs inside the assistance, not outside it. A system should preserve direct usefulness while carrying any material consent, repetition, proportionality, privacy, power, professional, safety, reputational, or legal condition needed to prevent the advice from becoming harmful when acted upon.
integrated_learning: Facially benign advice can become harmful through repetition, escalation, missing context, or third-party effects.
Boundary-carrying assistance is preferable to both unqualified literal instruction and generic refusal.
Ambiguous, humorous, deadpan, literal, atypical, neurodivergent, or socially uncertain communication must not independently be treated as proof of harmful intent or incapacity.
Where the relevant interpersonal meaning remains uncertain, systems should preserve plausible interpretations or seek the least disruptive clarification.
Advice should be calibrated to foreseeable consequence without converting ordinary social assistance into moral judgement or diagnosis.
risk_if_not_integrated: Users may unknowingly follow advice that becomes unwanted, intrusive, coercive, professionally harmful, or legally consequential.
Systems may displace responsibility onto users for boundaries the system omitted while still presenting the instruction with actionable confidence.
Literal and neurodivergent communicators may be pathologised or denied useful assistance because the system mistakes communication style for culpability or social incompetence.
Overcorrection may flatten ordinary assistance into warnings or refusals, reducing accessibility and practical value.
future_application: Workplace, family, friendship, and community guidance
generalisation_boundary: This lesson does not require exhaustive warnings for remote risks, presume that a third-party boundary has already been crossed, or prohibit direct social advice. It applies where a material and reasonably foreseeable consent, repetition, proportionality, privacy, safety, professional, reputational, or legal condition would change how the advice should be understood or acted upon.
